haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine's output goes to the shadow store.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes invoices into the shadow store and never calls the payment provider.
haiku-low.q3: Gate A: each of the last 7 consecutive days under 0.1% mismatch, with at least 5,000 invoices compared. On-call promotes, and the rollout tool checks comparison_results.
haiku-low.q4: The billing monitor starts it automatically when the new engine's payment-call failure rate exceeds 2% over 10 minutes. This applies only in both and new_only, not shadow.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. To take over again, on-call must promote to shadow and gate A must be met from scratch.
haiku-low.q6: After 35 days in new_only, the rollout tool rejects all rollbacks. Usage events are kept only 35 days, so the old engine cannot catch up.
haiku-low.q7: Workers read billing_mode at each invoice start, so an in-progress invoice finishes in its starting mode. They read charging_paused before every payment call, so a pause applies at the next charge.
haiku-low.q8: In comparison_results rows written nightly. The rollout tool checks them before writing billing_mode and refuses any promotion that skips a mode or fails its gate.
haiku-low.q9: The billing monitor measures the new engine's payment-provider call failure rate over a sliding 10-minute window. Above 2% in both or new_only, it starts a rollback and pages on-call.
haiku-low.q10: Due invoices are written to the ledger as pending, not charged. Charging resumes only at resume_charging, after reconcile, when charging_paused is set to false. In-flight calls finish.
haiku-low.q11: Reconcile matches each new-engine invoice with the old engine's. Already-charged invoices with agreeing totals are marked settled and never charged again. Mismatches go to Finance review.
haiku-low.q12: Billing stays in rolling_back with charging paused, and the new engine never resumes charging. On-call is paged, and the safe-to-repeat step is retried from the rollback record.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine computes invoices into the shadow store.
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes into the shadow store.
sonnet.q3: Gate A must be met: each of the last 7 consecutive days has a mismatch rate under 0.1%, and together those days compared at least 5,000 invoices. On-call promotes (through the rollout tool).
sonnet.q4: The billing monitor starts it when the new engine's payment-provider failure rate goes above 2% over a sliding 10-minute window. This applies in both and new_only (not shadow). In new_only it works only within 35 days of entering new_only.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. To let the new engine take over again, on-call must promote to shadow, and gate A must be met from scratch (then gate B later after both).
sonnet.q6: After 35 days from when new_only began. Usage events are kept only 35 days, so catch-up only works while every event since new_only began is still in the log. The rollout tool rejects every rollback after that.
sonnet.q7: Workers read billing_mode at the start of each invoice. An invoice in progress finishes under the mode it started in.
sonnet.q8: In the comparison_results rows written nightly by the comparison job (plus the Finance sign-off recorded in the rollout tool for gate B). The rollout tool checks these before writing billing_mode and refuses promotions that skip a mode or fail the gate.
sonnet.q9: The billing monitor. It measures the failure rate of the new engine's payment-provider calls over a sliding 10-minute window. If it goes above 2% in both or new_only, it starts a rollback through the rollout tool and pages on-call.
sonnet.q10: Invoices that fall due are written to the ledger as pending instead of being charged (a call already in flight finishes). The old engine charges the pending invoices at the resume_charging step, when charging_paused is set to false.
sonnet.q11: In reconcile, each new-engine invoice is matched with the old engine's invoice for the same customer and period. If it was already charged and totals agree, it is marked settled and never charged again. If totals differ, it goes to the Finance review queue and is not re-charged automatically.
sonnet.q12: The rollout stays in rolling_back with charging paused, and the new engine never gets charging back. On-call is paged, and the step is retried from the rollback record (steps are safe to repeat). Charges are delayed, not dropped or doubled.
